PullRequest.Title: Engineering - Rerun failed tests in isolation and split integration CI steps
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Rerun failed tests in isolation so transient failures can recover without repeating successful tests, while keeping persistent failures and runner errors visible.

## Changes

- Select failed tests by full title and failed hooks by their owning suite in fresh Electron windows or Node processes. Fall back to whole files for more than 50 targets, root hooks with file attribution, or regex-literal greps.
- Require an observed pass in the correct file before clearing a failure. Retain Node's loader and unexpected-error checks regardless of grep filters, and report recovered failures as flaky.
- Add `--only-node-tests` and `--only-extension-host-tests` to the integration scripts. Split their GitHub CI steps so extension-host suites still run after node integration or Agent Host E2E failures.
- Enable two retries for node integration and Agent Host E2E in pull request CI, adjust timeouts, avoid replaying CI annotations in repeated failure summaries, and update selection tests and documentation.

## Validation

Passed on macOS:

- `node --test build/lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts` — 10 tests passed.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/common/uri.test.ts --reporter dot` — 42 tests passed through Electron.
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/base/test/common/uri.test.ts` — 42 tests passed through Node.
- `npm run eslint -- test/unit/node/index.js test/unit/electron/index.js test/unit/electron/renderer.js build/lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts test/integration/agentHost/runner.ts` — passed.
- `node --check test/unit/node/index.js`, `node --check test/unit/electron/index.js`, `node --check test/unit/electron/renderer.js`, and `bash -n scripts/test-integration.sh` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` and the normal pre-commit hygiene hook — passed.

Additional review-time validation used temporary fixtures: seven live scenarios per runner covered successful rescue, persistent failure, before/after hook failure, changing titles, unexpected errors, and third-attempt recovery. All returned the expected exit codes. The `--only-node-tests` integration entrypoint also successfully exercised a live Electron retry. Temporary fixtures were removed.

Windows/Linux execution, the full integration/E2E suites, and full builds/type checks were not run locally. No associated issue.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The nested scans, unbounded fallback target count, synchronous completion path, and CI retry enablement are explicit in the changed code. Exact wall-clock impact depends on how many failures a broad incident produces, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and short-lived arrays created while repeatedly filtering all passed and failed test records
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For T unique retry targets and P/F pass/failure records from the rerun, this executes O(T × (P + F)) scans; T is not bounded when the >50-target whole-file fallback is active.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased retry latency and CPU/GC pressure on broad-failure CI runs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The Electron retry path tracked failed files in sets and reconciled a rerun with set construction/membership work linear in the number of failed files; it did not rescan every test result for every failure target.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each pending target now independently filters the complete failure and pass arrays to rebuild per-file title collections after every rerun.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 770 adds construction of `failedTitles` by filtering the entire failure array inside the per-target callback; RIGHT line 772 similarly filters all passes. Before this diff, retry reconciliation operated on failed-file sets rather than a target/result cross-product.
Findings.Title: Index rerun results before matching failure targets
Findings.Impact: When a shared or infrastructure failure produces more than 50 unique failed tests/suites, `planRerun` deliberately reloads their whole files, so a recovered retry can report thousands of passes while `findPassedTargets` rescans that full result once per original target. This synchronous work runs before the Electron test process can finish and can turn a broad retry into quadratic CPU and allocation cost.
Findings.Evidence: `planRerun` falls back to whole files once `targets.size > MAX_RERUN_TARGETS`, but `findPassedTargets` then runs `result.failures.filter(...).map(...)` and `result.passed.filter(...).map(...)` inside the loop over every deduplicated target. The PR workflows enable two reruns for the full Electron and integration suites, making this path reachable on broad transient failures.
Findings.Recommendation: Pre-index passes and failures once per rerun by file (and title/prefix as needed), then resolve every target from those indexes so reconciliation remains O(P + F + T), including the whole-file fallback.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The nested iteration and its execution after every successful child report are directly visible, and the >50 fallback establishes a realistic unbounded target/result cardinality. Only the incident size and resulting duration are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and short-lived arrays created while repeatedly filtering all passed and failed test records
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For T unique retry targets and P/F pass/failure records from the child process, this executes O(T × (P + F)) scans; T is not bounded when the >50-target whole-file fallback is active.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased retry latency and CPU/GC pressure on broad-failure CI runs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The Node retry path tracked failed files in sets and reconciled child results linearly by failed file; it did not rescan every test result for every failure target.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each pending target now independently filters the complete child result's failure and pass arrays to rebuild per-file title collections.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 534 adds a full failure-array filter inside the per-target loop; RIGHT line 536 does the same for passes. The deleted implementation reconciled failed-file sets and had no target/result cross-product.
Findings.Title: Index rerun results before matching failure targets
Findings.Impact: When a shared or infrastructure failure produces more than 50 unique failed tests/suites, the fallback reruns whole files and can return thousands of pass records. Matching those records once per original target runs synchronously in the parent before the CI test step exits, so broad retries can spend quadratic CPU and allocation work after test execution.
Findings.Evidence: `planRerun` switches to whole-file mode above `MAX_RERUN_TARGETS`, while `findPassedTargets` performs full `result.failures` and `result.passed` filter/map chains inside the callback over all deduplicated targets. All three PR workflows invoke Node tests and Node integration tests with two reruns.
Findings.Recommendation: Build per-file pass/failure title indexes once after reading the child report, then resolve targets from those sets so retry reconciliation is O(P + F + T).

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A single flaky test caused every test in each affected file to execute again in a fresh Electron window on every retry, repeating already-successful test work in proportion to file size.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Retry latency and CI resource use grew with all tests contained in failed files rather than with the actual failed tests; PR CI performs up to two retries.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The rerun plan now builds a title grep for up to 50 failed tests or failed-hook suites, so the fresh Electron window loads the required files but executes only the unresolved targets, retaining whole-file fallback for unsupported or broad cases.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 650, introduced by commit 0b9c9384fcec8f929335c8a95380e55f756c9465, constructed the next run from every failed file. The changed planner at line 756 creates a grep from deduplicated failed test/suite titles and passes it to the next window, directly removing execution of successful sibling tests for ordinary flaky failures.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful full Node and Electron unit-test runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Load the selected test modules, execute all tests, drain reporters, and exit. The changed pass bookkeeping is on this path, but retry planning is not reached when the first attempt succeeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Electron renderer emits Mocha pass/fail events to the main-process runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing IPC event per executed test; the diff enriches failure metadata and retains pass metadata but does not add event count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same pass/fail events crossed renderer-to-main IPC; pass records were not retained by the main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Events are consumed synchronously as tests run, but no new IPC round trip is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Node discovers/loads compiled test modules; Electron loads test resources and reporters may write result XML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Module/file work scales with the selected full suite and is unchanged by successful-run retry logic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full suite and reporter boundaries ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Test loading and reporter drain must complete before exit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of executed tests in the full suite; each pass adds one title/file record until process or window completion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each Node or Electron test step runs its runner serially; the platform workflows schedule the Node and Electron steps separately rather than introducing per-test concurrency here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CI starts cold processes/windows and module state is reused only within that attempt. The diff adds no persistent cache or cache key; pass records are attempt-local and released on exit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: pass-record creation and lifetime are explicit; there is no evidence that this linear bookkeeping alone creates a reportable regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact count and bytes retained by pass metadata vary with suite size and title length, but the added work is linear and modest relative to loading/executing the suite.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding for the normal path. The added per-pass metadata is linear, attempt-scoped, and does not change boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: A flaky or broadly failing Node/Electron unit or integration test run is retried
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the first failure, the runner builds a plan, starts a fresh Node process or Electron window, waits for selected tests and reporters, reads the result, reconciles pending targets, and only then exits. Reconciliation is synchronously on the retry critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn a fresh Node test process for a retry plan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one child per attempt and two retry children in PR CI; file arguments are deduplicated by the plan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Retries already spawned a fresh child, but executed every test in each failed file rather than selecting ordinary failures by title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: spawnSync serializes the parent behind the complete child run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write, read, parse, and delete the temporary JSON child-result report.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One report per Node retry, containing all passes/failures produced by selected or fallback files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A smaller failed-file JSON report existed; the diff changes it to pass/failure records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The parent cannot reconcile or exit until the report is read and parsed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and run a fresh Electron BrowserWindow for each retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One window per attempt, at most two retry windows in PR CI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Whole failed files were rerun in a fresh window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The loop awaits all tests and reporter drains before reconciliation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is unique failed tests, failed-hook suites, or files after map deduplication. At up to 50 targets title selection narrows executed tests; above 50 targets whole files run and may produce pass/failure arrays covering thousands of tests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Node retries use one blocking spawnSync child at a time; Electron retries use one fresh window at a time. Workflows allow at most two additional attempts. There is no concurrency limiter issue on these two runner paths, but reconciliation repeats per target.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every retry uses a fresh process/window, so in-memory module and runtime caches are cold. There is no result cache; target maps carry only retry state between attempts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: both changed findPassedTargets implementations rescan complete pass/failure arrays for every deduplicated target, yielding O(T × (P + F)) work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Broad transient failures are less common than isolated flakes, and exact P/F/T counts vary, but the fallback explicitly admits more than 50 targets and full-suite workflows provide a realistic large result set.
Scenarios.Verdict: Two findings reported, one per runner, for quadratic post-retry reconciliation. The ordinary <=50 title-selected path also records an internal regression fix because it removes pre-existing whole-file repeated execution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull-request Electron integration tests split into Node and extension-host steps
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a normal run, Agent Host E2E (when selected), Node integration, then extension-host suites complete sequentially before later workflow steps. On a Node integration failure, the new conditional still runs the extension-host step rather than aborting the combined script.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/pr-darwin-test.yml:Run extension host integration tests and corresponding Linux/Windows steps
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch a second integration script process dedicated to extension-host suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional shell/batch process per enabled OS job; script startup creates a temp directory and settings file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One script process ran Node and then extension-host suites, and set -e/errorlevel stopped before extension suites when Node failed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On successful runs it replaces the extension-host portion formerly executed inside the first script, adding only script setup. On Node failure it intentionally extends the job to collect extension-host results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch Electron/Node extension test processes for each selected extension-host suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same fixed suite launch count on successful full runs; on Node-failure runs these launches now still occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same launches followed a successful Node integration run in the combined script; they were skipped after a Node failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each suite is awaited serially and dominates the extension-host step duration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/remove temporary user-data directories and read compiled extension outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Temp setup now occurs once in each of two script invocations instead of once, while extension artifact reads remain per suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One temp user-data setup served both portions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Minor setup is on step startup; compiled extension reads are required by the tests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Node integration suite plus the fixed set of extension-host suites (api, language, git, notebook, standalone CSS/HTML/JSON), filtered only by explicit script options.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The GitHub steps remain sequential in each OS job. Extension-host suites run serially inside the script; splitting steps does not parallelize them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each script invocation creates a fresh temporary user-data directory. There is no shared warm application cache guaranteed across the two steps; compiled extension artifacts are prepared once by the preceding workflow step and reused from disk.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: workflow ordering and script process/suite launch cardinality are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact shell/setup overhead is platform dependent, and failure-path extension execution can consume minutes, but the latter is the explicit diagnostic goal of splitting the steps.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Normal-path expensive suite cardinality is unchanged, and the extra work after a Node failure is a deliberate bounded scheduling tradeoff to preserve independent test results.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host E2E suites fail, retry, and print consolidated failure details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The runner launches up to five suite processes, buffers each output, waits for completion, prints it, and extracts failure details. New workflow flags permit each failing suite process to perform up to two fresh-window retries before its parent suite process completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch per-entrypoint Agent Host E2E test scripts and their Electron retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to five suite processes concurrently; on failure each selected test runner may launch at most two additional Electron attempts because the workflow now forwards --rerun-failed-files 2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Suite processes ran with the same five-worker cap but workflows did not request failed-test retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each lane waits for its suite process and internal retries; the aggregate runner completes after all selected suites.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider/conformance E2E operations performed transitively by selected test entrypoints.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Depends on selected failed tests; title-level retries reduce ordinary repetition, while whole-file fallback can repeat a provider entrypoint. Runner concurrency remains capped at five.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same tests performed their remote operations once; the workflow now permits bounded repeats only after failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Any remote operation inside a retried test must finish before that suite lane completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Split/filter/join buffered failure output to suppress repeated CI commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or two linear passes over output for each failed suite result; output was already fully buffered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Output was split and scanned, but annotation lines were not filtered and the no-marker fallback reused the original trimmed string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after a failed child closes before consolidated reporting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected Agent Host E2E entrypoints after profile selection; concurrency is capped at five. Retry multiplicity is bounded to two extra attempts per failing suite, while output processing scales linearly with buffered log bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to five suite processes concurrently, controlled by the existing worker count/AGENT_HOST_E2E_JOBS. Retries occur inside those lanes rather than creating unbounded aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each retry intentionally uses a fresh window, so in-memory state is cold. Electron download selection is checked before suite execution and is not repeated by the changed failure-detail filter.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for process/output cardinality and worker cap. There is insufficient evidence that the extra linear annotation filtering is material relative to E2E execution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure frequency, remote test duration, and log volume vary; retries can lengthen a failing job substantially but are explicitly capped and intended to recover transient failures.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. Retry fan-out is bounded by existing workers and two attempts, and the output transformation is linear; both support the PR's stated failure-recovery/reporting behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and all diff pages. Reported the duplicated quadratic retry-result reconciliation in Node and Electron, and recorded the PR's ordinary title-level rerun path as a fix for the prior whole-file repeated-work regression. Other changed costs are bounded or intentional scheduling tradeoffs.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
